title: A steady stimulus can fade from awareness while the receptors still answer
summary: Sensory adaptation is no longer noticing a stimulus that stays constant, even though the receptors are still responding.
body: OpenStax Psychology says people often do not perceive stimuli that remain relatively constant over a long time. It calls that sensory adaptation. The chapter's example is a ticking clock that is obvious on entering a room and then drops out of awareness during conversation, while the auditory receptors are still affected. The example shows sensation and perception coming apart. The text is CC BY 4.0.
